events.continuity_hook: Returns to the Indianapolis lab after the main hotel and return-travel choices were made, with onsite access now driving the final logistics.
events.interaction_goal: Settle the Friday morning ground-transport plan, confirm how Kara will move the extra demo bag, and verify the hotel arrival and Sunday return still fit the lab schedule.
events.scenario_brief: About ten days before the Indianapolis seating and mobility lab, the clinic moves Friday check-in to an access-controlled rehab tower and asks Kara to bring one extra demo bag. She has the better-rated suite hotel and a Sunday afternoon return in place, with the hotel reconfirming a queen room, coffee maker, mini-fridge, indoor pool, and fitness room, but no hot tub. The remaining issue is whether an early rideshare will be dependable enough for a 7:00 a.m. onsite start or whether a small rental car is worth the added parking and equipment handling.

events.continuity_hook: Continues the Indianapolis pre-trip checks after ground transport was nearly settled, with the flight timing now creating the main decision.
events.interaction_goal: Compare keeping the shortened connection against switching to the later nonstop, then reselect a window seat if the updated seat map allows it.
events.scenario_brief: A week before the Indianapolis departure, the airline shortens Kara's Thursday connection and moves her outbound seat assignment back to unassigned after an aircraft swap. A later evening nonstop is available but would get her to the hotel close to midnight, while the current connection is still legal but leaves little room for a delay. The hotel can hold the room for either arrival time, and the clinic confirms Friday access instructions are unchanged.

events.continuity_hook: Starts a personal active-weekend episode after several fall work trips, using the lighter December window before January teaching picks up.
events.interaction_goal: Build a practical travel-and-hotel shortlist, compare driving against flying through Atlanta, and identify which hotel can handle a post-race shower or late checkout.
events.scenario_brief: After the Indianapolis lab clears, Kara's partner registers for a mid-December trail race outside Chattanooga. Kara can leave Tampa after a Friday morning debrief and needs to be back Sunday night or very early Monday to prep for a teaching block. Flying into Atlanta with a rental car avoids the longest drive but adds airport timing, while driving from Tampa is cheaper but turns Friday into a late arrival. Lodging splits between a race-area lodge with older room details and unclear refrigerator availability, and better-rated downtown suite options with clearer in-room basics and recovery amenities but a longer race-morning drive.

events.continuity_hook: Continues the Chattanooga active-weekend planning after race timing and room details narrow the lodging and return choices.
events.interaction_goal: Choose the lodging base, decide whether to fly-and-rent or drive, and book the room and return plan while the cancellable suite rate is still available.
events.scenario_brief: The race organizer posts Friday packet pickup from 4:00 to 7:00 p.m. and confirms the Sunday course closure should finish by 1:00 p.m. The race-area lodge now only shows double-bed rooms and still cannot confirm an in-room refrigerator, while a downtown suite hotel has a queen room, coffee maker, mini-fridge, indoor pool, hot tub, and fitness room, though it adds a parking fee and a 25-minute race-morning drive. Sunday afternoon flights from Atlanta are workable if they leave Chattanooga soon after lunch; driving the whole route keeps control but makes the return tiring.

events.continuity_hook: Starts a new winter work-trip episode as the fall travel wave winds down and January hosts begin locking instructor dates.
events.interaction_goal: Compare Wednesday outbound routes, the two hotel strategies, and Saturday versus Sunday return timing, then list what the hospital must confirm before Kara commits.
events.scenario_brief: A Denver-area children's hospital asks Kara to teach a mid-January pediatric neurodevelopment course on Thursday and Friday, with optional Saturday morning consults still being discussed. She can leave Tampa after a Wednesday morning class and needs enough recovery time before a Monday remote teaching block. Winter weather makes connection risk part of the flight comparison. The hospital-adjacent hotel has solid recent feedback and the shortest commute, but refrigerator availability is by request and it lacks a hot tub; a better-rated suite hotel about 15 minutes away has a queen room, coffee maker, mini-fridge, indoor pool, hot tub, and fitness room, but adds parking and possible snow-related drive time.

events.continuity_hook: Continues the Denver course after the host clarifies Saturday timing and equipment storage, making the itinerary bookable.
events.interaction_goal: Select the flight pattern, choose between the hospital-adjacent hotel and the suite hotel, and book the itinerary with a window seat if the seat map is open.
events.scenario_brief: The Denver host confirms the Saturday consult block will end by noon and can receive Kara's demo materials two days before she arrives. A Wednesday nonstop from Tampa arrives before dinner but costs more than a one-stop option through Dallas; the Saturday late-afternoon return is possible but leaves little cushion if consults run long or roads are slow, while a Sunday afternoon return adds one hotel night and protects her Monday readiness. The hospital-adjacent hotel can guarantee a queen room and coffee maker but still cannot guarantee a refrigerator, while the suite hotel confirms the fuller room and recovery setup.
